shifts.summary: Candidates described the paper as overall moderate, with most reporting it as such. Good attempts ranged from about 61 to 80 questions across all sections. Time pressure was a common issue, especially in Quant where many long percentage, area and trigonometry items appeared. General Awareness featured policy questions such as Swachh Bharat and Rigveda, while English included synonym‑antonym and passage items.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was seen as easy by some and difficult by others, timing was a concern for many candidates.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA included several policy‑related items and current‑affairs questions from 2025‑2026.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math had many lengthy percentage, area and trigonometry questions, causing time shortage.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was generally easy, with synonym‑antonym, one‑word substitution and passage items.

observations: Time pressure was noted especially in Quant, candidates could attempt about 15‑16 questions.
Math section had many long percentage, area and trigonometry questions, leading to insufficient time.
General Awareness featured policy‑related questions such as Swachh Bharat and Rigveda.
Overall paper was considered moderate by most candidates.
disagreements: Reasoning was reported as Easy by 2 reports and Difficult by 2 reports; GA was Easy in 1 report and Difficult in 2 reports; Quant ranged from Moderate to Difficult in 1 report and Difficult in 3 reports; English ranged from Easy to Moderate to Difficult across reports.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 23 October 2026 showed a generally moderate difficulty level according to the limited review available for shift 1. Candidates noted time pressure, especially in Quantitative Aptitude, and highlighted topics such as policy questions in General Awareness and synonym‑antonym items in English. Any figures reported, such as the number of attempted questions, are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Shifts 2 and 3 have not yet yielded usable analysis, and further candidate evidence is required before a comprehensive review can be published.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Based on the partial review for shift 1, the exam was described as moderate by most candidates. This assessment is limited and should be corroborated with additional evidence.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates reportedly attempt on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Some candidates mentioned a range of attempts, but the numbers are unofficial and not reliably confirmed. The exact figure remains uncertain pending further verification.

faqs.q: Which sections caused the most time pressure on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Time pressure was most commonly reported in the Quantitative Aptitude section, where many long‑form percentage, area and trigonometry items appeared. English and General Awareness also featured time‑intensive items.
